source.work: Pattern-Oriented Software Architecture Vol 1 (Buschmann et al., 1996); Microsoft Application Architecture Guide (2009)
source.paraphrase: In strict (closed) layers, a layer may only call the layer immediately below it; presentation calls business/application logic, never persistence or the database directly.

invariants.why: Presentation code that directly imports persistence bypasses domain invariants and couples the UI/API to the database schema.
invariants.fixHint: Call the service or use-case in the application/business layer instead of importing the repository directly.
invariants.avoid: Using dynamic import(), type-only re-exports or path aliases to reach the persistence folder directly from a controller.

source.work: Patterns of Enterprise Application Architecture (M. Fowler, 2002)
source.locator: Unit of Work / Transaction Script in Service Layer
source.paraphrase: Transaction boundaries belong to business operations in the application or domain service layer, not to HTTP controllers or UI presentation.

invariants.why: Opening or committing database transactions in presentation code leaks infrastructure lifecycle into the UI layer.
invariants.fixHint: Demarcate transaction boundaries in the service or use-case layer.
invariants.avoid: Calling $transaction, beginTransaction, commit, or rollback directly within controllers or routes.
